title: Data retention zones & deployment pathways - Oakmont Financial intake
summary: Initial compliance and hosting discovery to map Oakmont's data residency, log retention limits, and deployment model preferences (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is evaluating tradeoffs for PII/HIPAA-like workflows and strict financial audit controls.
topics: GDPR data subject and cross-border transfer concerns
HIPAA-adjacent controls for patient-like data in financial fraud team
Log retention, redaction, and access auditability
Private/VPC deployment requirements and key management
Latency and cost tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated
next_steps: Redwood: Share SOC2 + encryption-at-rest whitepaper and KMS integration doc (Priya, due 2027-03-22)
Customer: Provide high-level list of data types considered PII and retention windows (Karen, due 2027-03-25)
Schedule technical deep-dive for Private deployment networking with Diego and Marcus (target week of 2027-03-29)
action_items: Priya Patel: Send SOC2 report and Private deployment checklist (due 2027-03-22)
Marcus Lee: Prepare short note on KV cache purging and log redaction options (due 2027-03-26)
Karen Holt: Circulate PII inventory and retention policy excerpts (due 2027-03-25)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Karen Holt (Oakmont Head of Compliance), Diego Ruiz (Oakmont Platform Eng), Sana Ibrahim (Oakmont ML Infra), Tom Wells (Oakmont Procurement)

Summary: Quick intake to understand Oakmont's compliance boundaries, what data they will send to an LLM, and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private is the right fit. Client emphasized strict log retention and redaction requirements and wants clear evidence trails for auditors.

[00:00] Priya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, really appreciate you taking the time today
[00:08] Karen: thanks, yeah we wanted to get a sense of where Redwood sits on residency and audit trails before we go deeper, so thanks for setting this up
[00:15] Diego: hi all, i'll mostly listen but i'll ask network questions around VPC and peering, low latency between our apps and the model endpoints is important
[00:24] Marcus: great, i'll handle technical stuff, priya will cover contracting and compliance docs; quick agenda, high level compliance constraints, deployment models, logging/retention expectations, then next steps

[00:42] Karen: to start, our use case: fraud detection and transaction enrichment. we'll be sending transaction-level metadata, sometimes names and masked account digits. some of this is considered sensitive under our internal policy — we treat it like PII/HIPAA sensitivity for audit purposes, even if not healthcare. so two primary asks: 1) we need proof logs are resident in the region and 2) we need the ability to redact or never persist certain fields in logs

[01:10] Priya: understood. for residency, we support hosted regions with region locking and Dedicated or Private if you want customer-only compute. We also have controls for log forwarding and redaction. can I ask — do you have a strict no-cross-border-transfer rule or is it permissible with SCCs or equivalent safeguards?

[01:30] Karen: it's not binary, um — for EU data we prefer it stays in EU infrastructure. For US accounts the issue is more about access controls and audit trails. We can't have raw PII stored in logs for more than 30 days, and some audit artifacts must be kept for seven years but with redaction applied first

[01:52] Sana: slightly more detail from the infra side — our pipelines attach user identifiers to certain events. If the model runtime keeps KV cache entries or request logs those must either be redacted at ingest or encrypted and accessible only by our compliance teams via KMS with rotation policies

[02:10] Marcus: yeah so two separate pieces: first, request/response logs and second, runtime caches like KV caches. For Hosted, by default we keep ephemeral runtime state and configurable request logs. For Dedicated we offer dedicated GPU pools and a control plane that can be region-limited. Private gives you everything on-prem or in a VPC with your own KMS

[02:32] Tom: cost is a factor — Private is attractive from a control viewpoint but procurement needs clear TCO and SLAs. Can you speak to typical cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for stable throughput?

[02:45] Priya: rough rule of thumb — Dedicated is higher baseline cost but gives predictable throughput; Hosted is lowest TCO for variable loads. Private is highest because of infra and ops overhead. We'll share a pricing band and a sample TCO run for a typical fraud enrichment workload

[03:05] Karen: ok, but from compliance — we need immutable audit logs showing who accessed what. Are access logs stripped of PII by default or do you store raw payloads?

[03:20] Marcus: by default, request payloads can be sent to logs depending on account settings. For enterprise customers we support log redaction at ingest and token-level cost/latency breakdowns without storing full payloads. We can also forward logs to your SIEM instead of storing them in our control plane

[03:41] Sana: forwarding to SIEM sounds promising — we run Splunk and would like to maintain our own retention policies there. Any connectors or recommended patterns?

[03:50] Marcus: yes we have webhook/forwarding connectors and an S3 sink option. For Dedicated and Private, forwarding is typically used so Redwood stores minimal metadata but you keep full audit trails. The S3 sink can be encrypted with your KMS key

[04:09] Diego: technical question — if we do Dedicated in eu-west-1, is the control plane still Redwood-managed in us-east or do you offer a private control plane for EU only? Network constraints mean we sometimes can't have control plane traffic crossing geographies

[04:27] Priya: good question. Hosted Dedicated still uses Redwood control plane but we can region restrict data and control-plane operations. For strict control plane residency we offer Private with customer-managed control plane in the VPC or on-prem

[04:46] Karen: auditors will ask for proof of where keys live. we need KMS integration details and whether keys can be customer-managed and rotated on schedule

[04:55] Marcus: we support external KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for encryption at rest, though control plane metadata may remain in Redwood's region unless Private is chosen

[05:12] Tom: any certifications or third-party audits you can share? SOC2? ISO?

[05:18] Priya: yes SOC2 type II reports, ISO 27001 scope docs, and a security whitepaper we'll send. For Private, particular audit evidence may be scoped differently since infra is customer-managed

[05:30] Karen: good. back to retention windows — sample scenario: we need raw logs for 30 days then fully redacted versions kept for 7 years for audit. How would Redwood support that workflow?

[05:45] Marcus: several options — 1) redact at ingest: strip PII fields before logs reach Redwood. 2) store raw logs in your S3 bucket (encrypted) and short-lived copies in Redwood for 30 days, then purge; 3) store redacted audit artifacts in our long-term retention with access controls. We can combine forwarding and lifecycle policies to achieve the 30-day/7-year combo

[06:10] Sana: is there support for automated redaction rules? we have a list of regexes and fields we consider sensitive

[06:18] Marcus: yes we have ingest-time filters and an SDK for client-side redaction, plus server-side field masking rules for common patterns. There may be edge cases where transcription is imperfect, so we recommend a two-layer approach: client-side sanitize + server-side policy enforcement

[06:38] Karen: what about e-discovery requests — auditors may demand the full unredacted record for specific events under legal process, can we request that?

[06:48] Priya: for Hosted, by default Redwood does not retain unredacted records longer than configured retention. If you need legal hold access to unredacted data, Dedicated or Private is better because you control where raw logs are stored. We can support a secure workflow but it must be designed up front and documented in the contract

[07:10] Diego: network-level: for Private, we need to do VPC peering and control plane endpoints. Do you support private peering or Transit Gateway patterns?

[07:20] Marcus: yes private endpoints are supported; we commonly use either VPC peering or PrivateLink-like endpoints. We'll document port requirements, CIDR ranges, and the recommended NAT/egress patterns for updates

[07:36] Tom: procurement will want an exit plan — if we stop using Redwood, how do we get our logs and models and what is the retention handoff?

[07:45] Priya: we provide an export of logs and metadata; for Dedicated/Private we can include a handover runbook. We'll include retention export options in the SOW and specify timelines for data purge after contract termination

[07:58] Karen: any third-party subprocessing? where do you have cloud providers and which subprocessors have access to logs?

[08:08] Priya: we use cloud providers in each region; we maintain a subprocessor list and publish it in the security docs. For EU data, we can limit subprocessors and provide contractual assurances

[08:20] Diego: small performance question — will redaction at ingest add latency? our fraud scoring is latency-sensitive

[08:27] Marcus: minimal if done client-side. Server-side redaction adds small overhead; we have async patterns where we return responses immediately and handle redaction/logging asynchronously to keep critical path latency low

[08:42] Sana: can you talk about KV cache persistence? we need assurance that the KV cache is ephemeral and not written to long-term storage

[08:50] Marcus: KV cache is in-memory by default and not persisted to disk for Hosted/Dedicated. In Private deployments, the runtime can be configured to persist to customer-managed storage if requested. We'll provide configuration knobs and lifecycle docs

[09:08] Karen: ok auditors will want a cert or attestation that KV cache isn't retained, is there an established audit language for that?

[09:16] Priya: we'll provide an operations attestation and include config settings in the audit package. For Dedicated we can get closer to your needs; Private gives you the most control and easiest auditor sign-off

[09:30] Tom: what's the recommended path for starting? Pilot on Hosted with redaction set, or go straight to Dedicated?

[09:38] Priya: depends on risk appetite. Many customers pilot on Hosted with strict client-side redaction and forwarding to their SIEM to validate workflows. If you need long-term residency or auditor-proof separation up front, Dedicated or Private is recommended. We can run a short pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate latency and retention behavior

[09:57] Karen: let's say pilot on Hosted but with strict redaction and logs forwarded to our Splunk, and concurrently scope Dedicated for a 6-month plan if pilot shows sustained throughput. Is that reasonable?

[10:10] Priya: totally reasonable. action items — we'll send compliance docs and a private deployment checklist, Marcus will add notes on redaction and KV cache, and you will share the PII inventory

[10:22] Diego: ok i'd like the deep-dive technical session to include network diagrams and sample IAM policies for the Private control plane

[10:30] Marcus: noted, i'll prepare sample diagrams and an IAM template

[10:36] Karen: one more quick point — we also have subsidiaries in APAC, later we'll need region isolation there and proof-of-residency in ap-southeast-1, so keep that in mind

[10:47] Priya: noted, we support multi-region and can geo-lock models and storage per tenant

[10:55] Tom: procurement question — can you share a sample SOW and termination clauses around data export?

[11:02] Priya: yes we'll include an SOW template with exit/data export clauses in the next email

[11:10] Sana: any differences in SLA between Dedicated and Private?

[11:14] Marcus: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Private SLAs depend on the infra model — if Redwood manages the private control plane we can offer SLAs, if fully on-prem it's reliant on your ops

[11:30] Priya: ok we'll recap by email. thanks everyone — next steps: Priya sends docs, Marcus schedules technical deep-dive, Karen shares PII inventory.

[11:45] Karen: thanks, that was helpful
[11:47] Dieg o: thanks
[11:48] Priya: thanks all, bye

End of transcript
